description:
## Goal

Implement Filament.Hooks.use_memo/2. Returns a memoized value recomputed only when its
dependency list changes. Use this to avoid re-running expensive computations on every render.

Depends on: C1 fully merged. Can run in parallel with C2.

## Deviation policy
Any deviation from this spec requires prior approval. Stop work, run
'bw comment flm-oue.3 "..."' describing the conflict, reopen the ticket, and await guidance.

---

## Where to add the function

FILE: lib/filament/hooks.ex (created in C1)

Add to Filament.Hooks:

  @doc """
  Returns a memoized value recomputed only when deps changes.

  On the first render, always calls fun.() and caches the result.
  On subsequent renders, compares deps to the previously stored deps using structural
  equality (Kernel.==/2, which is Erlang term equality). If deps is equal, returns
  the cached value. If deps changed, calls fun.() and caches the new result.

  deps should be a list of values that the computation depends on:
      expensive = use_memo(fn -> Enum.sort(large_list) end, [large_list])

  Pass [] as deps to compute only once (on mount). Pass :no_deps to recompute every render.

  Rules: call only at the top level of render/1.
  """
  @spec use_memo((-> result), deps :: [term()] | :no_deps) :: result when result: term()
  def use_memo(fun, deps) when is_function(fun, 0) do
    {index, previous, _ctx} = use_slot(:__unset__)

    {value, stored_deps} =
      case previous do
        :__unset__ ->
          # First render
          {fun.(), deps}

        {cached_deps, cached_value} ->
          if deps == :no_deps or cached_deps != deps do
            {fun.(), deps}
          else
            {cached_value, cached_deps}
          end

        _other ->
          # Unexpected slot content (e.g., slot reused by hook order change) — recompute.
          {fun.(), deps}
      end

    commit_slot(index, {stored_deps, value})
    value
  end

  # Convenience: allow use_memo(fn, single_value) as shorthand for use_memo(fn, [single_value])
  # Do NOT implement this convenience now — keep the API strict.
  # Future: use_memo(fn -> ... end, some_value) raises a clear error if deps is not a list or :no_deps.

The stored slot value is {deps, value} — a 2-tuple. use_slot reads this from the previous
render's hook_slots. commit_slot writes the new {deps, value} for the next render.

---

## Edge cases to handle explicitly

1. deps == [] — only compute on first render. After first render, previous is {:__unset__ was replaced}
   so deps comparison [] == [] is always true and fun.() is never called again.

2. deps == :no_deps — recompute on every render (pass-through, no caching).

3. fun.() raises — do NOT catch the exception. Let it propagate and crash the render.
   The LiveView supervisor will handle the crash.

4. use_memo called with wrong arity (e.g., fun/1) — Elixir type system catches this at
   compile time if the caller passes a named function. Anonymous fns with wrong capture arity
   produce a clear Elixir error. No special handling needed.

---

## Tests

Create test/filament/use_memo_test.exs. All tests use the with_render_ctx helper from
test/support/hooks_helpers.ex (created in C1).

  1. First render — fun.() is called, result returned
     - Simulate render with no existing fiber
     - use_memo(fn -> :computed end, [:dep])
     - Assert returns :computed

  2. Second render, same deps — fun.() is NOT called
     - Simulate first render: use_memo with counter-tracking fn (increment Agent counter)
     - Simulate second render with same deps: assert counter not incremented

  3. Second render, different deps — fun.() IS called
     - Same setup, second render with different deps: assert counter incremented

  4. deps == [] — fun.() called only on first render
     - Three consecutive renders, assert fun.() called exactly once

  5. deps == :no_deps — fun.() called on every render
     - Three renders, assert fun.() called three times

  6. use_memo and use_state in same render — slot indices don't collide
     - Simulate render: call use_state(:x) then use_memo(fn -> :y end, [])
     - Assert state slot is 0, memo slot is 1
     - Second render: both return correct values

  7. fun.() raises — exception propagates out of use_memo unmodified
     - use_memo(fn -> raise RuntimeError, "boom" end, [])
     - assert_raise RuntimeError, "boom", fn -> ... end

## Acceptance criteria

- mix test test/filament/use_memo_test.exs passes (7 tests)
- mix compile --warnings-as-errors passes
- The slot value format {deps, value} is internal to Filament.Hooks — not part of
  the public API and not leaked to application code
- use_memo does NOT send messages to the LiveView (it is purely synchronous, no side effects)
